prs.title: docs: clarify fork remote setup
prs.author: Ankit Pandey
prs.body:
## What

Clarify the fork remote configuration for first-time contributors.

## Why

Contributors can accidentally fetch from or push to the upstream repository after cloning a fork. The guide now shows an explicit `origin`/`upstream` setup and verification step.

## How

Adds copyable Git commands to `CONTRIBUTING.md` for renaming the cloned remote, adding the contributor fork as `origin`, fetching upstream, and syncing `develop`.

## Testing

- `git diff --check`
- Documentation-only change; no runtime tests required.

prs.title: fix(utils): aggregate non-Error promise rejections without crashing
prs.author: fadi romdhan
prs.body:
## Summary

**What** — `promiseAll(..., { aggregateErrors: true })` no longer throws a `TypeError` when one of the promises rejects with something that is not an `Error` (`undefined`, `null`, a string, a number). The aggregated message now uses `reason?.message ?? String(reason)`.

**Why** — `getMessageError` read `state.reason.message` unconditionally. prs.title: fix(medusa): report a failed migration script instead of exiting 0
prs.author: gautamyash
prs.body:
Summary

What — What changes are introduced in this PR?

db:migrate now checks the exit code of the db:migrate:scripts child process and returns false (non-zero exit) when a migration script fails, instead of discarding the exit code and returning true regardless.

Why — Why are these changes relevant or necessary?

db:migrate forks db:migrate:scripts as a child process, but never checked its exit code — unlike the db:migrate:search call a few lines above, which already does. A migration script that throws logs the error but the parent process still exits 0, so any CI/CD pipeline or deploy step that trusts medusa db:migrate's exit code carries on as if every script succeeded, even though the database may be left partway through. Fixes #17033.

How — How have these changes been implemented?
